references.text: Kadesh-Barnea is mentioned here as the place where the spies returned, the same place that marks the southern boundary in Num 34:4.
Kadesh-Barnea is mentioned as the starting point when the spies were sent out to explore the land.
Kadesh-Barnea is described as the place Israel reached after traveling through the great and fearful wilderness.
Kadesh-Barnea is mentioned as the starting point of Israel's journey before they crossed the Zered Brook.
Describes Judah's southern boundary with the Ascent of Scorpions (Maaleh-Akrabbim) and Kadesh-Barnea, the same boundary markers as in Num 34:4.
Mentions Azmon as part of Judah's southern boundary, the same place as Atzmona in Num 34:4.
The Ascent of Scorpions (Maaleh-Akrabbim) is mentioned as a boundary marker for the territory of the Amorites.
Ezekiel's vision of the future boundaries of the land includes Kadesh and the Wilderness of Sin as the southern boundary marker.
